title: The passive in all tenses
tagline: Turning the sentence around so the action — not the person who did it — comes first.
exam: Reading & Use of English Part 4 — key word transformations
Reading & Use of English Part 2 — open cloze (be / been / being)
Writing Part 2 — report or article: describing processes and results
why: News reports, rules, instructions and results usually don't care who did the action — they care what happened. The passive lets English do that without an awkward somebody or they. B2 First checks it across every tense, with two-object verbs, and in fixed patterns like is said to that turn a whole opinion into one clause.

diagrams.title: The passive pattern
diagrams.caption: Whatever received the action becomes the subject; the person who did it becomes optional.

diagrams.title: Active to passive, step by step

before.text: Cambridge English administers the B2 First exam in over 130 countries.

after.text: The B2 First exam is administered by Cambridge English in over 130 countries.

steps: Move the object of the active sentence (the exam) to the front, as the new subject.
Put be in the same tense as the original verb: administers → is administered.
Add the original subject after by only if it's useful information: by Cambridge English.

rows.label: Example
cells: People say the new coach is very strict.
It is said that the new coach is very strict.
The new coach is said to be very strict.

rows.label: Use
cells: formal, sounds more like a fact about the subject

head: Tense / form
Structure
Example
rows: The gym is being repainted this week.
The mural was designed by three students.
The hall was being cleaned when we arrived.
The trophy has been moved to the main office.
The tickets had already been sold by Monday.
The winners will be announced on Friday.
The essay must be handed in by Thursday.

use.point: Focusing on the action or the result, not on who did it

examples.text: The new library was opened last September.
examples.note: the opening matters, not necessarily who cut the ribbon

examples.text: Over three hundred entries have been received for the poetry competition.
examples.note: the number matters more than who sent them

examples.text: Mistakes are usually corrected before the final draft.
examples.note: a general process, agent unknown or unimportant

use.point: Naming the agent with by, only when it adds real information

examples.text: The mural was painted by a group of Year 12 students from Arequipa.
examples.note: the agent is the interesting part of the sentence

examples.text: The announcement will be made by the head teacher herself.
examples.note: worth mentioning because it shows importance

examples.text: The data was collected by sensors placed around the school garden.

use.point: Verbs with two objects: two possible passive subjects

examples.text: Nadia was given a certificate for the best project in the fair.
examples.note: the person (indirect object) as subject — the more natural choice

examples.text: A certificate was given to Nadia for the best project in the fair.
examples.note: the thing (direct object) as subject — possible, but less common

use.point: Reporting opinions, and combining the passive with modals

examples.text: It is said that the school will introduce a new uniform next year.
examples.note: impersonal passive for a general rumour

examples.text: The coach is thought to be considering Liam for the first team.
examples.note: personal passive — sounds like established fact

examples.text: The final version should be submitted before Friday at noon.
examples.note: modal + passive: an instruction, not a statement of fact

watch_out.wrong: The letter was wrote by the head of department.
watch_out.right: The letter was written by the head of department.
watch_out.why: The passive needs the past participle (written), not the past simple form (wrote).

watch_out.wrong: The homework must finished by Monday.
watch_out.right: The homework must be finished by Monday.
watch_out.why: A modal passive always needs be before the past participle.

watch_out.wrong: The trophy was given to by the mayor.
watch_out.right: The trophy was given to the winning team by the mayor.
watch_out.why: Don't double up the preposition — to introduces the receiver, by introduces the agent, and both aren't needed together like that.

watch_out.wrong: It says that the results come out on Friday.
watch_out.right: It is said that the results come out on Friday.
watch_out.why: The impersonal reporting pattern needs the passive: it is said, not the active it says.

watch_out.wrong: The photos were took by a student from the club.
watch_out.right: The photos were taken by a student from the club.
watch_out.why: Use the past participle taken, not the past simple took, after were.

dialogue.title: The mural competition results
dialogue.context: Sofia, Liam and Nadia are reading the noticeboard outside the art room, where the results of the interschool mural competition have just gone up.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Look — the winners were announced this morning while we were in class!

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Our mural was chosen for the coastal wall, near the main gate.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Really? It is said that the judges loved the recycling theme.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: And apparently the paint is being donated by a local hardware shop — we don't even have to buy it.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Nice. When is the wall going to be prepared? It needs a proper base coat first.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Miss Vega said it will be sanded and primed by the maintenance team on Thursday.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Then we 'll be given the whole weekend to paint it, I think.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Perfect. And a plaque with our names is going to be added next to the mural, apparently.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: That's brilliant. This project has never been done at our school before.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Exactly why it should be taken seriously — let's not mess it up.

items.sentence: The new science block ___ next year.
This song ___ by a group of students from Cusco.
items.why: past passive needs the participle written

items.sentence: The gym floor ___ at the moment, so PE is in the hall.
items.why: an action in progress → present continuous passive

items.sentence: All entries ___ before the deadline on Friday.
Liam ___ a medal for the best design.
items.why: passive with a two-object verb, person as subject

items.sentence: It ___ that the trip will be moved to October.

practice.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct passive form of the verb in brackets.

items.sentence: The results ___ (publish) on the website every June.
The mural ___ (paint) by three students last term.
The classroom ___ already ___ (clean) when we got there this morning.
New laptops ___ (order) for the computer lab right now.
The final decision ___ (make) by the committee next week.

summary: Build the passive with be in the right tense + past participle; only add by + agent when it matters.
The passive exists in every tense and after every modal — is done, was being done, has been done, must be done.
Verbs with two objects usually make the person, not the thing, the subject of the passive: She was given a prize.
It is said that… and X is said to… turn a vague they say into a more formal, impersonal report.
Choose the passive when the receiver of the action, or the action itself, matters more than who did it.
